blocks.source: Sublimis inter aera Ignatius tenetur: Quando te ulgens sidera precando conatur Apostolos in judicium ab legat hinc vereptum: Cum caeteris exotiicum hic, excolit rosetum. Aufert suorum cordibus sodalium pavorem Cum Christus ipsis omnibus proponit et favorem.

Ignatius is held aloft in the air;
[The printed “Quando te ulgens sidera precando conatur” is unresolved.]
[The printed “Apostolos in judicium ab legat hinc vereptum” is unresolved.]
With the others, here he cultivates [the printed “exotiicum” is unresolved] a rose garden.
He removes fear from the hearts of his companions,
When Christ sets before them all favour.

blocks.source: Haec vota supplex offero Ignatio praesenti, Et hunc honorem defero majora potenti. Exopto per te maximi nunc ponderis favorem, Tum Numinis, tum proximi terris in his amorem. Ut mens soluta corpore festaret ad superna, Et pace pleno pectore fruatur cive aeterna.
blocks.english:
A suppliant, I offer these vows to Ignatius present,
And render this honour to him who can do greater things.
Through thee I now desire a favour of the greatest weight:
Love both of God and of my neighbour here on earth;
That the mind, freed from the body, might keep festival in regard to things above,
And with a breast full of peace might enjoy an eternal female citizen.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. Festaret is an attested postclassical festare (keep festival), not an emended haste verb; lexical evidence https://mateo.uni-mannheim.de/camenaref/nolte/nolte1/Nolte_lexicon_3-1.html. Cive is regular ablative singular of common-gender civis; aeterna specifies feminine. Literal female citizen retained without changing source to heavenly city or eternal life. The unexpected devotional imagery is not a defective Latin form. Prior prepared English/provenance archived; Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish:
A suppliant, I offer these vows to Ignatius present,
And render this honour to him who can do greater things.
Through thee I now desire a favour of the greatest weight:
Love both of God and of my neighbour here on earth;
That the mind, freed from the body, may hasten unto things above,
And with a breast full of peace may enjoy [the printed “cive aeterna” is uncertain].

blocks.source: Salve Sancte Patriarcha Ignati, imitator Jesu Christi; templum Spiritus Sancti; serve amantissime SS. Trinitatis! Salve emulator Martyrum; imago Apostolorum, Vas electionis. Salve expugnator vitiorum, compendium virtutum, idea perfectionis. Salve norma patientiae; castitatis lilium, modestiae speculum. Salve obedientiae prodigium, charitatis ignis, pauperum refugium. Salve exemplar abstinentiae, humilitatis prototypon, afflictorum solatium. Auxiliare Magister ignorantium, dux poenitentium, reformator Christi; norum illumina mentem meam, dux infidelium Guberna cor meum, magne affectuum tuorum moderator. Impetra mihi veniam, felicissimae pacis conciliator. Excra in bono perseverantiam, firma Ecclesiae columna. Intercede pro me, meisque omnibus, tum consanguineis, tum amicis et benefactoribus; strenue clientium tuorum Protector. Sis mihi scutum in adversitatibus; defende me in tentationibus, et omnibus in vita malis, nec me deferas in hora mortis meae. Amen.
blocks.english: Hail, holy Patriarch Ignatius, imitator of Jesus Christ, temple of the Holy Ghost, most loving servant of the most Holy Trinity! Hail, emulator of the Martyrs, image of the Apostles, vessel of election. Hail, conqueror of vices, compendium of virtues, pattern of perfection. Hail, rule of patience, lily of chastity, mirror of modesty. Hail, marvel of obedience, fire of charity, refuge of the poor. Hail, example of abstinence, model of humility, comfort of the afflicted. Help, teacher of the ignorant, leader of penitents, [the printed “reformator Christi; norum” is unresolved]; illumine my mind, leader of unbelievers; govern my heart, great moderator of thine affections. Obtain pardon for me, bringer of most blessed peace. [Printed Excra: unresolved verb] perseverance in good, firm pillar of the Church. Intercede for me and all mine, both kinsfolk and friends and benefactors, vigorous protector of thy clients. Be my shield in adversity; defend me in temptations and from all evils in life, and carry me not away at the hour of my death. Amen.

blocks.source: Ego Dominus vocavi te in justitia, et apprehendi manum tuam, et servavi te, et dedi te in foedus populi; in lucem gentium, ut aperies oculos caecorum, et educeres de conclusione vinctum, de domo carceris sedentem in tenebris.
blocks.english: I, the Lord, have called thee in justice, and taken thy hand, and preserved thee, and given thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the nations, that thou shalt open the eyes of the blind, and mightest bring forth the prisoner from confinement, and him that sits in darkness from the prison house.

blocks.source: Oremus, Deus, qui servum tuum S. Ignatium de mundi caesis ad spiritualis militiae triumphos evocasti; praesta quaesumus: ut eum sequamur lucem morum, et protectorem consequamur. Per Christum Dominum nostrum.
blocks.english: Let us pray. O God, who didst call Thy servant Saint Ignatius from the slain of the world to the triumphs of spiritual warfare, grant, we beseech Thee, that we may follow him as a light of conduct, and obtain him as a protector. Through Christ our Lord.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. Caesis is the substantive ablative plural perfect participle of caedo, the slain, governed by de; mundi is genitive. No unprinted castris or standard biographical battlefield wording substituted. Prior prepared English/provenance archived; Latin unchanged.

Vespers has only its printed versicle; no response is invented.
